title: Protected type rigid flange coupling
parts_note: two flanged hubs, one sunk key per shaft, and n bolts; the bolt count comes from the shaft size
verify_note: The CHECKS are verified against two independent sources; the PROPORTIONS are not, and cannot be. Leutwiler 1917 article 275 gives the same three failure groups this tool checks (key by shear or crushing, bolts by shear or crushing, flange shearing off at the hub) and his equations (413) and (414) are algebraically identical to bolt_shear and bolt_crushing here. NPTEL module 4 lesson 1 gives the two key equations, which key_shear and key_crushing match. On the proportions Leutwiler is explicit: no uniform proportions of flange couplings had been proposed for adoption as a standard, and published tables are individual manufacturers' practice. So the ratios below are a convention, not a standard, and that is why this flag stays false.

bolt_stresses_mpa.source: bolt material, usually weaker than the shaft, UNVERIFIED

rim_height.note: how far the protecting rim stands proud, times d

shaft_length.note: shaft stub shown each side, times d

units: SI: mm, N, MPa. First angle projection (Indian practice, SP 46).
books_searched: Unwin 1899 page 234 does give a flange coupling table (n = 3 + 0.5 d, bolt diameter = 0.62 d / sqrt(n), a = 1.5 x bolt, c = 1.25 x bolt, b = 0.25 d + 0.125, t = b/2) but it is an 1899 design in inches, with an absolute term in b, and it is not the protected type this tool builds. It was read and rejected, not skipped. NPTEL Design of Machine Elements I (course 112105125) has no couplings module: its modules are 4 joints, 7 springs, 8 shafts, 10 permanent joints, 11 joints for special loading, 12 brakes. Do not search that course again.
verified_parts: The two key checks ARE verified: NPTEL module 4 lesson 1 gives shear over the whole key and bearing over HALF the key thickness, which is what key_shear and key_crushing do. The empirical proportions below are what remain unverified.
checks_verified_against: Leutwiler 1917 art. 275 eq. (413) bolt shear, eq. (414) bolt crushing; NPTEL IIT KGP module 4 lesson 1 for the key in shear and in bearing over half its thickness.
